How can I become a more disciplined person?
Keep a list of the things you want to do. Visualizing things, and actively seeing what you're not accomplishing can help. It did for me.

When I have something (potentially annoying) to do, I try to focus on the result and how glad I'll be when it's done. I project myself on my future mood and state of mind, like "this will take 2 hours, but then I'll have the satisfaction that I no longer need to do it", and I think about how relaxed I will be, free to do whatever pleases me afterwards.

Doing what you have/want to do is rewarding so I know my future me will feel better (and relieved) very soon, it makes me want to do what I' be decided.

My problem are the things that take much longer. IE: Saving up money for a downpayment on a house, forcing myself to do homework when I still have 2 years left for finish my degree, etc...

Short term goals are fairly simple for me to tackle. Staying focused on the long term is what really requires discipline. Short term is more about motivation, I believe.

Alright I understand your point. I don't have specific advice for this but I think it's important to keep track of your goals, and the progress you make to see that you're reaching your targets, step by step.

It's good that you're coming out of your shell, contributing, even slightly, I think is better than just lurking in the distance, your voice can be heard and you can attend to things that matter to you without fear of being backlashed here.

A few tips:

  • Rudeness and insulting someone because you disagree with them doesn't help anybody. Things to ask yourself when you reply to a comment you disagree with:

Did I bring up everything I needed to bring up with sources?

Did I insult the other user or type anything out with pure irrationality?

Could I make my response more detailed to make it appear more elaborate and mold it to be more convincing?

Just some thoughts on that part.

  • Speak your mind when you comment, don't worry about what everyone else is thinking, this makes sure a "hivemind" doesn't grow too big on here like it has on reddit, this doesn't mean let's be discourteous to others, but it just means that you should be yourself and not adhere to what the hivemind says unless you genuinely agree.

I heard a streamer (Santorin maybe?) say something along the lines of, "I'm not going AP Eve, I would do that if I was trying to carry from the jungle." I hadn't really thought of doing an AP Eve build before. AD/Tanky seemed more reliable, and it was ok from what I've played before. But I played some AP Eve and it was crazy. I'm in Silver and these are normal games so take that into account, YMMV.

I started out rushing Runeglaive, then Mobi's and Rylai's. The new Rylai's means you can pretty much perma slow with your spamming Q and the tankiness helps. After that, Luden's Echo and usually GA and then gunblade. Those are all expensive items but I got so fed it didn't matter. The reason you don't see Rylai's is because I sell it for a Rabadon's when I get 6 items. You don't need the slow so much anymore if you can pop them, plus you're fighting as a team anymore at that point. Of course I build for the enemy team, too. Notice the Randuins for the AD heavy team, Mercurial Scimitar for Warwick ults and Abyssal for AP heaviness.

I'm gonna be sad when Runeglaive gets nerfed to only work on monsters. Only once after getting it in all of my games did I ever go oom. Eve was bad at longer engages due to her mana issues spamming spells but this fixed it completely.

Here are the results of my games. My back hurt a lot after that last one :( https://slimgur.com/image/fT4
